page: Amazon Web Services m5a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the fifth-generation AMD-powered EC2 lineup. Running on the lightweight AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance is equipped with an AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 8 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, establishing a standard 4 GB per vCPU distribution. The instance includes no attached local instance storage and relies on network volumes, accompanied by a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and no bundled public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the first-generation Zen architecture of the AMD EPYC 7571 in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute performance. Stress-ng tests yield single-core throughput of 590.59 and multi-core output of 1,179.96, while Geekbench scores reach 725.0 single-core and 1,744.0 multi-core. Cryptographic routines benefit from dedicated hardware instructions including AES and SHA-NI, resulting in an average PassMark encryption score of 3,248.98 despite a modest overall PassMark CPU score of 3,670.17. Memory subsystem testing reflects 154.42 GB/sec cached read throughput, decreasing to 30.01 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 14.45 GB/sec for large-block writes.

From an operational and resource allocation standpoint, m5a.xlarge delivers predictable dedicated thread execution and a balanced memory-to-core allocation without the premium associated with compute-heavy or newer processor generations. However, the absence of AVX-512 extensions and modest single-thread speed limit its capability in intensive vector computations, machine learning inference, and high-throughput data processing. Static web serving reaches 2.98 GB/sec and Redis key-value operations achieve 2.51 million SET operations per second. Consequently, this server profile is best matched with steady-state general enterprise workloads, staging servers, small relational databases, code compilation pipelines, and containerized microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m5a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an AMD EPYC 7571 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, accompanied by 16 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The configuration includes no onboard local storage, requiring external network block storage for persistence, and features a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. In performance benchmarks, the AMD EPYC processor registers lower-tier computational results, scoring 725 in Geekbench single-core and 1,744 in multi-core metrics, alongside 3,670.17 in PassMark CPU tests. Hardware acceleration for AES and SHA instructions delivers average encryption performance, reaching 3,248.98 on PassMark encryption tests. This profile offers cost-effective, dedicated resources suited for lightweight web serving, internal enterprise applications, basic microservices, and development environments.
